messages:
Nora Kim: FYI — we started seeing a p99 jump for inference in eastus2 around 11:40 UTC. From ~120ms -> ~330ms.
Ben Patel: saw the alert. Any packet loss or retransmits in the east-west path?
Nora Kim: yes, traceroutes show intermittent drops between gpu-host-12 and gpu-host-45. Packet loss ~1-2% for short bursts.
Maya R.: I can confirm latency spikes correlate with some tc churn events in the host bootstrap logs.
Nora Kim: here's the tail of the host-init log that coincides with the first spike:

```
Mar 16 11:39:12 host-init[1]: applying network shaping
Mar 16 11:39:12 host-init[1]: tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 30
Mar 16 11:39:12 host-init[1]: tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 1gbit
Mar 16 11:39:12 host-init[1]: tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 u32 match ip dst 10.10.0.0/16 flowid 1:1
```

Ben Patel: hmm that filter looks like it was intended to prioritise infra traffic but the match ip dst 10.10.0.0/16 is our GPU pod CIDR — it's effectively forcing HTB shaping on east-west pod traffic.
Ash Singh: Also, HTB + clsact interactions can drop skb when RDMA/cluster offloads are in use. We saw similar with TSO/GRO offload earlier.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout completed: infra-bootstrap v2.14.1 to eastus2 (by infra-ci)
Nora Kim: that matches timing. So a bootstrap change accidentally applied host-level HTB for pod CIDR.
Maya R.: quick repro on a dev host: when HTB class rate << nic capacity we see queueing and small sustained packet loss -> inference p99 climbs.
Ben Patel: mitigation options: 1) remove the tc rule from hosts (fast rollback), 2) adjust filter to exclude pod-to-pod traffic for GPU CIDR, or 3) add a bypass class with higher priority.
Ash Singh: patching now to remove the filter and restart network stack on a canary host.
Nora Kim: commands being run on canary (Ash):

```
# remove offending filter
sudo tc filter del dev eth0 parent 1:0 prio 1
# delete HTB qdisc
sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root
# verify
tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
```

Maya R.: can you also check ethtool offloads? If offloads were disabled it could exacerbate CPU copy which increases latency.
Ash Singh: checked — offloads intact. After qdisc removal canary p99 returned to ~130ms and packet loss dropped to ~0.01%.
ops-bot: infra-ci: rollback job queued for infra-bootstrap v2.14.0 -> v2.14.1 reverted in eastus2
Ben Patel: rolling this to the rest of the cluster. We should also add a test in bootstrap that rejects shaping the GPU CIDR unless explicitly opted-in.
Nora Kim: agreed. Postmortem: owner Maya. Action items: 1) block default HTB for pod CIDR in host-init, 2) add unit/integration test in provisioning CI, 3) add observability: tc-change audit metric, 4) run a short e2e stressing KV cache to validate p99 before rollout.
Maya R.: I'll open the postmortem and add the checklist. Also will add an alert rule for sudden host qdisc changes.
Ben Patel: nice triage. Anyone want to add notes about RDMA? We should document that classful qdiscs can interfere with ibverbs paths.
Ash Singh: added note to infra playbook: avoid adding shaping on NICs with RDMA-active routes; prefer off-node egress shaping at ToR if needed.
Nora Kim: thanks team — monitoring shows regressions cleared. Assigning to Maya for next-week follow-up and adding to release checklist.
